nodes.title: README — H3 Character Sheet Maker
widgets_values:
# H3 Character Sheet Maker

Turn up to **9 reference images** into a clean six-view character sheet in a single generation.

Feed it a face, an outfit, a weapon and a hat, and H3 will assemble them into one coherent character,
then show you that character from four sides plus two face close-ups.

---

## Why a video model

Six separate image generations of the same character will disagree with each other — the jaw shifts,
the jacket changes, the palette drifts. Six frames from **one** video generation physically cannot,
because they share a single denoising pass.

This workflow renders one continuous 360° orbit, pulls six frames out of it, and stitches them into a
sheet. No hard cuts anywhere, so nothing gets a chance to reinvent itself between shots. The camera
does all the moving; the character stays frozen.

---

## Quick start

1. **Load your references.** Any mix of photos, drawings or anime art. The first one sets the style.
2. **Fill in `Input Text (Prompt)`** — one line per image saying what to take and what to ignore.
3. **Pick your size** on the Resolution Selector: aspect ratio, then megapixels.
4. **Leave duration at 5.** Everything downstream is tuned to it.
5. Queue. The finished sheet lands in `ComfyUI/output/charsheet/`.

---

## The two prompt boxes

They get joined together automatically, so you only ever touch the first one.

**`Input Text (Prompt)`** — yours. Assign every image one job and one ignore list:

```
<Picture 1> - keep the photo style. Use the bald head, facial hair, physique.
<Picture 2> - keep only the black outfit. Remove the hair, remove accessories.
<Picture 3> - use the shield. It is attached to the man's back.
```

Being blunt about what to *ignore* matters as much as what to keep. Backgrounds, poses and the wrong
person's face all travel across unless you rule them out by name.

Describe fabrics and materials **in words** too. Faces carry across on their own; wardrobe drifts.
"Black high-collared coat with silver buckles" survives where "the outfit from `<Picture 2>`" wanders.

**`Prompt for orbiting`** — the fixed half. Backdrop, lighting, lens, the A-pose, the statue lock and
the three beat timings. Leave it alone unless you're changing the shot structure, and if you do, see
*Retiming* below.

---

## What you get

| # | View | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Front | orbit 0% |
| 2 | Left side | orbit 25% |
| 3 | Back | orbit 50% |
| 4 | Right side | orbit 75% |
| 5 | Face, front | beat 2 |
| 6 | Face, three-quarter | beat 3 |

Laid out 3 wide × 2 tall with thin black gutters.

---

## Settings worth knowing

**Duration — leave at 5.** That's 124 frames. Valid lengths are `17n + 5`: 5, 22, 39, 56, 73, 90,
107, 124. Anything else rounds up. 124 puts the orbit at roughly 100°/s, an ordinary turntable speed.
Go much shorter and the spin outruns the model — it smears past about 5° per frame.

**Aspect ratio.** Portrait for people. 9:16 wastes the least frame on a standing figure.

**Megapixels.** 0.5 to scout, 0.7 for normal use, 1.2+ when you want the face crops to hold up. Cost
scales roughly linearly, so prove the composition cheap before you commit.

**Speed-up nodes.** Sage Attention and caching both cost some prompt adherence here. Deliberately left out. Add them if you like.

**Optional outputs.** Two extra save nodes are bypassed by default: every individual frame, and the
raw video. Un-bypass either if you want to cherry-pick your own angles.

---

## Getting good results

**Give it a back view if you have one.** With only front-facing references the entire back of your
character is invented. This is the single biggest quality lever in the workflow, and no amount of
prompt tuning substitutes for it.

**Watch for flutter.** Hair and cloth want to move. The fixed prompt already freezes them hard; if
something still ripples, name the specific offender in your input box.

**Assembling from many sources?** If the character is built from three or more images, consider two
stages: run once to get a clean front view, then feed *that* render back in as `<Picture 1>` and
build the sheet from it. A purpose-made reference beats a pile of contradictory ones.

**Retiming.** The six grab points are locked to the beat timings in the fixed prompt. If you change
those times or the duration, open the subgraph and move the frame indexes to match, or the grabs will
land mid-transition.

---

## Then what

Use the character sheet how you would like. You can input it as a reference for future H3 video generation, use it for custom DnD character, use it for visualizing characters or props.

nodes.title: Prompt for orbiting - (Keep Picture 1's Style)
widgets_values:
[STYLE]
The output is matches the style of <Picture 1>. Sharp detail on eyes and face. The style never changes and never drifts between shots. No shadows.


[STAGING]
Solid light grey seamless backdrop, one flat uniform tone edge to edge, with no gradient, no vignette, no texture and no floor line. Nothing else is in frame. the subject casts no shadow onto the backdrop and no contact shadow on the ground beneath it, and it does not sit in its own shadow. Soft form shading on the subject itself is fine and should read its shape. Long telephoto lens, near-orthographic.

The character holds one relaxed A-pose throughout: arms hanging slightly away from the body, palms toward the thighs, feet shoulder-width apart, head level, calm neutral expression, eyes open and looking forward.
The subject is completely frozen, as rigid and motionless as a statue. Only the camera moves. There is no wind, no breeze, no air movement, no breathing, no settling, no sway, no secondary motion of any kind. Orientation, surfaces and lighting are identical in every shot, and the subject stays the same size in frame.

[0-3 seconds] tight full shot of the subject. The camera makes one smooth fixed-speed orbit right around it, a full 360 degrees: starting square on the front, passing the left side a quarter of the way round, directly behind at halfway, the right side three quarters of the way round, and returning to the front. The subject does not move at all. Ends back on the front view at 3 seconds.

[3-4 seconds] Camera snaps into a fast push-in on the character's face. Locked-off head and shoulders close-up, face square to camera, eyes into the lens. Ends on a sharp front-on face.

[4-5 seconds] camera whip-pans and rotates to a orthogonal angle. Locked-off head and shoulders close-up, head turned to a three-quarter angle, eyes still forward. Ends on a clean three-quarter face.

[CAMERA] One constant-speed orbit in beat 1, then locked off and static. The camera is the only thing in the scene that moves at any point. No zoom, no push in, no dolly, no tilt, no roll, no handheld shake, no motion blur, no dissolves.
[AUDIO] Silence. No music, no room tone, no voices.

nodes.title: Note: Speed Patches (PlagueKind V6 tuned)
widgets_values:
## Speed stack — matched to PlagueKind MiniMax-H3 V6

Order (same as his): **SLA -> LowVRAM Attn -> ChunkFF -> TorchSettings -> Turbo LoRA -> AdaLN Fix -> Sigma Shift**

1. **H3SLAAttention** (PlagueKind Nodes) replaces the old `SLAAttention` + `ModelAttentionBackend` pair.
   The dense backend (`comfy_kitchen`) is set *inside* this node, so nothing overwrites it and no
   separate attention-backend node is needed. His V6 note: "I've added my Sparse attention node. No other speedups required."
   - `sparsity_ratio` 0.90 = his default. 0.80-0.85 ~ pytorch quality. 0.95 = big win on long/hi-res, minor degradation.
   - `min_seq_len` 4096, `dense_last_steps` 1, `dense_steps` 0, `protect_audio` on, `stabilize_motion` on, `disable_fp16_accum` on.
2. **MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention** head_chunks 4 — new, from his loader.
3. **FP16 Accumulation** now **off** (was on). The SLA node sets accumulation itself; leaving both on fights it.
4. **Chunk FeedForward** 2 / 4096 (was 4 / 4096).
5. **Turbo LoRA** left on your `ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1 @ 1.0` since this graph is Ref2V.
   His is `H3/turbo/minimax_h3_fl2v_lightx2v_v0.1_dareties_v4_step600_comfy_fro.safetensors @ 0.8`.
   If you swap to that one, **enable node 6** below.
6. **H3AdaLNLoRAFix** (`port`) — bypassed by default. Required by the dareties turbo LoRA.
   Needs `models/h3_adaln/h3_silu_temb_grid.safetensors`.
7. **Sigma Shift** 8 / 3 (was 12 / 3) — his values.

Sampler outside this subgraph: euler + **simple** + 8 steps (was beta). He explicitly avoids EasyCache — it costs visible quality.

Requires: ComfyUI-PlagueKind-Nodes, ComfyUI-KJNodes. The marduk191 SLA-sage pack is no longer needed.
